title: Shopify Product Variants — Options, Selectors, Deep Linking & UX
content: Official Shopify product variant guidelines (from shopify.dev). Products can have a maximum of three options, and a single combination of options is a variant (e.g. Size: S + Colour: Black = one variant). CORE OBJECTS: product object and variant object. DEEP LINKING: Two URL formats: (1) ?variant=[variant-id] targeting specific variant. (2) ?option_values=[id-1],...,[id-N] selecting by option combination. Key attributes: selected_variant (returns deep-linked variant), selected_or_first_available_variant (fallback to first available). VARIANT SELECTORS: Present each option separately in the UI — do not use a single combined selector. Leverage product.options_with_values to generate individual selectors for each option. Use JavaScript to manage state changes. When a new variant is selected, product media and price must update to reflect the selection. PLACEMENT: JSON or Liquid product templates, product grid snippets, or quick view components. Dawn theme reference: product-variant-picker.liquid and global.js. PRODUCT MEDIA: Supported types — images, 3D models, uploaded video, external video (YouTube, Vimeo). Use Liquid objects: external_video, video, video_source, model, model_source. Support preview images for all media types. AR functionality available for 3D models. PRODUCT RECOMMENDATIONS: Two intents: (1) Related products — auto-generated by Shopify, shows similar/substitutable items ('You might also like'). (2) Complementary products — manually set up by merchant via Search & Discovery app, shows items that pair well ('Pair it with'). Track effectiveness from Analytics page in Shopify admin. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Design variant selectors as separate option groups — one row of colour swatches, one row of size pills, etc. Never combine options into a single dropdown. Design the selected state, disabled/unavailable state, and hover state for each option value. For colour variants, design as swatches (small circles or squares with the actual colour fill). For size/material variants, design as pill buttons. Always show a visual connection between variant selection and the product image — when user selects a colour, the main image should visually correspond. Design the out-of-stock variant state (greyed out, strikethrough, or dimmed). Include a recommendations section in your product page design — a horizontal scrollable row of 4–6 product cards labelled 'You might also like' or 'Pair it with'.
